newsitem.title: ITALY: Reform plan clears Italy Senate by huge majority.
newsitem.headline: Reform plan clears Italy Senate by huge majority.

text.p: Italy's Senate (upper house) voted overwhelmingly on Thursday to set up a special commission of both houses of parliament to draft reforms to the country's 1948 constitution, parliamentary officials said.

The vote, by 256 to 16 with two abstentions among members present, was well in excess of the two-thirds majority needed to adopt the plan without a referendum. The proposal now goes to the lower Chamber of Deputies for a similar vote next week.

The plan won the required broad support after parties in the main centre-right opposition Freedom Alliance buried internal differences on Tuesday and announced they would back the proposed commission.

It won similar strong support on a first reading in both houses last year but hard right leader Gianfranco Fini, whose party is the second biggest in the Freedom Alliance, had since campaigned against it.

The commission of 70 members will be drawn equally from both houses of parliament and will have until June 30 to draft proposals on how to make Italy's system of government and parliament more efficient and on federal devolution.

The Freedom Alliance and the governing centre-left coalition remain sharply divided on many of the issues, especially on the balance of power between government and parliament. Proposed reforms will be sent to parliament for debate.
